title: Squeeze: The Estimation Duel 2.0
body: Squeeze 2.0 is a brand-new game world. A bridge in the clouds, a fox and a dog, and a number line that zooms with your every move — from a sliver of a claim to the whole sky when someone was WAY off. Type your claim, then slide your guess along a line that runs from 0 to infinity (or type it): no ceilings, no hints, any number goes. WATCH: the fox and the dog play one short round for you before…
source: App Store release notes, US storefront

body: Photos that always fit the question. title: Squeeze: The Estimation Duel 1.4
body: A whole new look — and your face in the game. Every question now opens on real scenery: over 1,700 questions play on their actual place (the Colosseum on the Colosseum, Amsterdam on its canals), and every other question gets a scene that fits its topic. A warmer, bolder design throughout: new type, a Home that opens on the game's scenery, and a reveal that lands with a golden pin on the answer.…
source: release copy in the product repo, dated by the commit that added it

title: Squeeze: The Estimation Duel 1.3
body: Squeeze now speaks French! Choose English or French the first time you open the app, and switch any time with the EN · FR button on the Home screen. In French, the announcer speaks French and every answer comes in kilometers, meters, °C and euros. 705 new questions about France and the French-speaking world. The most surprising ones show up in English games too. Better facts for everyone: we…

title: Retired
body: A crowdsourced data-collection API with an iOS capture app and an MCP server. I shut it down, paid everyone who had done work on it, and kept two lessons: measure demand before building supply, and never trust a health check that doesn't open a connection.
source: this site; the shutdown is recorded in the product's own repository

title: Vitality Weeks 1.3.4
body: The age-based facts have been rebuilt from the ground up. Every fact now has to clear one bar: you should recognise either the person or what they did. Thousands of forgettable entries were removed rather than kept for volume. What's left is around 12,000. At 10, Tatum O'Neal won an Academy Award. At 34, Kazuo Ishiguro won the Booker Prize. At 81, Alice Munro won the Nobel Prize in Literature. —…
source: App Store release notes, US storefront

title: The Distribution Moat in the AI Era
body: AI makes making things nearly free. When supply is cheap, the value moves to whoever owns the relationship with the people who choose. A short case, in the words of Ben Thompson and Lyn Alden.
